ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Its central named case addresses the immortal Lü Dongbin: after he asks about hiding a world in a grain and cooking mountains and rivers in a small pot, Huanglong Huinan points and says, “this corpse-guarding ghost” (這守屍鬼).
EvidenceBody: Lü invokes a drug of deathlessness; Huanglong Huinan replies, “even after eighty thousand ages, in the end you fall into empty extinction” (饒經八萬劫，終是落空亡). Other Chan records apply the same epithet to sitting inert on a cushion, a tenth-stage sage, and anyone who lives a hundred or thousand years but remains “a corpse-guarding ghost; its ghost does not disperse; a dead person” (守屍鬼魂、不散底死人). Yet Gaofeng Yuanmiao also instructs someone to guard on and on like a corpse-guarding ghost until the doubt-clump bursts with a sound. The Chan deviation is the use of this macabre epithet across case verdict, criticism, and an attested simile in instruction. The differing appraisals are preserved rather than harmonized.
